title: Dakar 2026 - Ethiopian Elsabet Amare Takes Her Racing Dreams from Injibara to Dakar
summary: [Bird Story Agency] Inspired by her father and Ethiopian distance-running great Meseret Defar, 17-year-old Elsabet Amare is preparing to represent her country at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games. The runner hopes her journey will encourage other young athletes from her hometown of Injibara.

title: Africa Urged to Strengthen Regional Power Integration for Energy Security
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Stronger regional electricity networks and effective power markets would enable African countries to utilize their energy resources more efficiently while improving the resilience of their electricity systems, United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA) Executive Secretary Claver Gatete said today.

title: Death of Three, Injuries of 20 Kenyans Attributed to Ethiopia's Moyale Conflict
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- A Kenyan woman was killed by a suspected stray bullet in the border town of Moyale on 2 November, bringing to three the reported number of Kenyans killed in conflict linked to ongoing clashes in Moyale of neighbouring Ethiopia, according to Kenyan media reports.

title: Rights Commission Confirms 48 Killed in Shirka Attacks, Raises Alarm Over Informal Armed Groups
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The Ethiopian Human Rights Commission (EHRC) has confirmed that 48 people were killed in attacks in Shirka Woreda, Southeast Oromia, on 24 October, corroborating the death toll Addis Standard reported on 26 October based on eyewitness accounts and residents who attended the victims' mass funeral.

title: Ethiopian-American Pleads Guilty to Spying for Ethiopia, Faces Up to 22 Years in U.S. Prison
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Abraham Teklu Lemma, a naturalized U.S. citizen of Ethiopian descent and former U.S. government IT contractor, pleaded guilty on November 3 to conspiring to transmit highly classified national defense information to Ethiopian government officials, potentially exposing him to nearly 22 years in prison.

summary: [HRW] Government Should Lift Ban, End Attacks on Media

title: Kenya Begins Registering Ethiopian Refugees Fleeing Moyale Clashes - Arrivals Surpass 50,000
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Kenyan authorities, in collaboration with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and the Kenya Red Cross Society (KRCS), have begun registering Ethiopian refugees fleeing renewed clashes in the border town of Moyale, as more than 50,000 people have reportedly crossed into Kenya since fighting intensified in late October.

title: Sudan Lodges Formal Complaints Against Ethiopia With UNSC, AU Peace and Security Council
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Sudan's army-aligned government has lodged formal complaints against Ethiopia with the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) and the African Union Peace and Security Council (AUPSC), accusing the country of allowing the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) to use Ethiopian territory to launch drone attacks against Sudan.

title: Ethiopia, China Pledge to Deepen Military and Strategic Cooperation
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia and China have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening their longstanding military and strategic partnership.

title: The Battle for Baidoa - Testing Somalia's Federalism and Limits of Presidential Power
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- In Somali politics, Baidoa is far more than the administrative capital of South West State. It is a strategic political center where clan representation, federal bargaining, regional autonomy, and the struggle for national power converge. Whoever commands political legitimacy in South West State possesses an important advantage in the broader contest over Somalia's political future.

title: Ethiopia's Governance Trajectory Shows 'Warning Signs' Despite Modest Gains: Ibrahim Index
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Ethiopia's overall governance performance improved modestly over the past decade, but worsening security, rule of law and rights indicators have placed the country on a trajectory marked by "Warning Signs," according to the 2026 Ibrahim Index of African Governance (IIAG).

title: Long After Ethiopia Completes GERD, Egypt, Sudan Invoke Nile Water Rights Under Colonial-Era Agreement
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Egypt and Sudan have renewed their opposition to Ethiopia's independent management of the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD), invoking historical Nile water-sharing agreements and demanding a binding legal framework, more than a year after Ethiopia officially inaugurated the project.

title: Woman Killed By Suspected Stray Bullet in Moyale Amid Ethiopia Conflict
summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- A 65-year-old woman has been killed in Moyale after she was struck on the head by an object believed to be a stray bullet amid ongoing clashes between two regions in neighbouring Ethiopia.

title: Contested Land, Historical Grievances - Tracing Borana Pastoralists' Territorial Loss and Roots of Moyale Conflict
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- In his 2001 study, "Participation and Governance in the Development of Borana: Southern Ethiopia," researcher Johan Helland noted that, historically, Borana territory extended well beyond present-day Ethiopia into areas of what are now Kenya and Somalia, reaching as far as the Tana and Juba rivers. This history points out that Borana Oromoo have a broad geographical territory and the importance of land for pastoral communities.

title: Survivors Flee Hayiq Jari IDP Camp After Deadly Drone Strike
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Displaced people are fleeing the Hayiq Jari 2 Turkey camp for internally displaced persons (IDP) in Amhara region following a deadly drone strike that killed at least 18 civilians and injured 22 others, with survivors reporting the closure of essential support services and growing uncertainty over where they can go.

title: Somaliland Officials Condemn Attacks On Oromo Residents in Borama After More Than 150 Homes Reportedly Damaged
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Somaliland officials and community leaders have condemned attacks targeting Oromo residents in Borama, where more than 150 homes belonging to the residents were reportedly damaged or looted, as authorities announced arrests and pledged legal action.

title: Sudan Says 70 Drone Attacks Launched From Ethiopia Killed, Wounded Hundreds Over Eight Months
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Sudan has accused Ethiopia of enabling drone attacks launched from its territory that killed or wounded hundreds of civilians and soldiers, saying it documented 70 attacks involving 187 one-way attack drones between 15 February and 27 October, according to a report by the army-led Transitional Sovereignty Council.

title: Oromia Says 73 Detained Over Arsi Killings As Residents Report Post-Attack Arrests
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The Oromia Regional Government says 73 individuals have been taken into custody in connection with deadly attacks in Shirka Woreda, Southeast Oromia, describing the arrests as part of security operations against what it calls "Tsimdo" and other armed groups, amid earlier reports of mass detentions of residents following the killings.

title: Authority Suspends Registration of Ethiopia's Oldest Independent Newspaper Indefinitely
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The Ethiopian Media Authority (EMA) has indefinitely suspended the registration certificate of Media and Communication Center PLC, publisher of the Amharic Reporter and English-language The Reporter newspapers, citing alleged repeated violations of the law and professional ethics.

title: Will Renewed Conflict Derail Ethiopia's Economic Growth?
summary: [DW] Ethiopia's economy is growing strongly. But renewed fighting in the north of the BRICS member state could deter investment, strain public finances and push up the cost of living.

title: Govt Relocates Two KCSE Centres in Moyale Over Kenya-Ethiopia Border Clashes
summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The Ministry of Education has relocated two national examination centres in Moyale Sub-County, Marsabit County, following insecurity triggered by clan clashes along the Kenya-Ethiopia border.

title: Emirates Businesswomen Council Sees Growing Investment Opportunities in Ethiopia
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Chairperson of the Emirates Businesswomen Council Aisha Mohammed Saeed Al Mulla has praised Ethiopia's growing business potential.

title: Geopolitical Rivalries, Economic Pressures and Climate Risks Dominate the Global Agenda
summary: [ENA] The final week of October 2026 underscored the increasingly interconnected nature of global affairs, as geopolitical rivalries, diplomatic efforts to contain conflicts, economic uncertainty and escalating climate risks continued to shape the international agenda.

title: Ethiopia Calls for Fairer Global Representation As Al Jazeera Marks 30 Years of Broadcasting
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia has reaffirmed its openness to Al Jazeera and other international media organizations, emphasizing its commitment to facilitating responsible journalism grounded in fairness, balance and accuracy.

title: Ethiopia Steps Up Preparations for Major African Health Conference
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia has entered the final stages of preparations to host the fifth Conference on Public Health in Africa (CPHIA 2026) in Addis Ababa from November 23 to 27, Health Minister Mekdes Daba said.

title: Violence in the North Is Pushing Health System to the Brink, WHO Chief Warns
summary: [UN News] The head of the World Health Organization (WHO) called on Monday for greater protection for civilians caught in conflict in northern Ethiopia following deadly drone strikes this past weekend.

Yet our experiences are evidence of what works, what does not, and what systems need to change. Listening matters, but it is only the beginning. What truly matters is whether our perspectives shape priorities, inform decisions, direct resources, and strengthen accountability.
